items.feedback: Right. What makes a system an agent is the loop: the model picks an action, the program runs it, and the result comes back for the next step. A longer prompt, a bigger model or more memory changes what one call can do, not that structure.

You picked 'the calendar entries, which it read by opening the booking system', as if the model reaches into the booking system itself. The model only writes text. Here that text is a request naming check_calendar with the laser cutter and tomorrow's date as arguments (option c). The program around the model runs the tool and sends the result back. It is tempting because the final answer looks as if the model checked the calendar itself.

Right. The agent is repeating itself and getting the same failure, so more steps add nothing. A step limit is the stopping condition that ends the loop and reports back to a person. A larger window would not help, since all 40 steps already fit.

The answer is 4, not 1. You wrote that the model runs the 3 tools itself within one call. The model never runs tools. Each call ends with one tool request or the final answer, so the 3 requests take 3 calls and the final answer takes a 4th. The program runs the tools between calls. A quick check is to count the inputs the model receives: the question plus 3 tool results.

'It sends it back to the model' is the right first half. The question also asks why. The program sends the result back as part of the model's next input and calls the model again, so the model can use it to pick its next step or write the final answer. Next time, add the purpose to the action.

Your first sentence is exactly right: the model is given each tool's name and a short description, and picks the one that fits the request. The second claim is wrong. The model does not remember which tool it picked in earlier sessions. Memory is not automatic. Each session starts fresh unless the program saves and reloads something. This matters for your assistant's training-status memory, which you will have to build.

summary: You have the core of the loop down: what makes an agent, the role of a step limit, and that the model chooses tools from descriptions. Two ideas need fixing. First, the model never runs a tool (q2 and q4). It writes a request, and the program runs the tool and feeds the result back. Second, the model has no automatic memory across sessions (q6). Next step: trace the laser-cutter request on paper as a table with columns 'model outputs', 'program does' and 'model receives', then recount the model calls. Quiz 0001 s2 (your retake) will show whether this has stuck.
